text:
rajesh: FYI onboarding smoke found a parity issue between ios-sdk and js/py: JSON-mode fncall responses with a discriminator field get stripped by ios helper, causing the schema validator to pick the wrong union branch. reproducible in sample-app v2.

emily: ouch. can you paste the minimal example?

rajesh: minimal schema: 
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "payload": {
      "oneOf": [
        { "type": "object", "properties": { "type": {"enum": ["A"]}, "a": {"type": "string"} } },
        { "type": "object", "properties": { "type": {"enum": ["B"]}, "b": {"type": "number"} } }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
raw model response (JSON-mode fncall): `{"payload": {"type":"A","a":"ok","extra":"x"}}`

rajesh: ios normalizer removed unknown fields (extra) but also dropped the discriminator `type` in one branch due to a bug in our sanitizer: it was doing a shallow copy and then filtering keys against the expected props but used the wrong prop set for the chosen branch. result arriving into validator looked like `{"payload": {"a":"ok"}}` which fails to match branch A (no type) and was picked as B by accident after fallback heuristics -> downstream crash.

maria: how do js/py handle unknown keys? do they preserve discriminator?

emily: js/py preserve unknown keys by default in json-mode sanitizer; they only strip when you pass strictSchema=true. ios had conservative behavior to avoid leaking unexpected fields into app, but it must never drop discriminators used for branching.

rajesh: fix proposed: when normalizing union branches, compute allowedProps for each branch and ensure discriminator keys (explicit enums or keys present in original response) are retained before filtering. fallback: if discriminator gets removed, abort normalization and return the raw object (preserve) so caller sees unexpected case.

maria: add unit test: union of two objects with enum discriminator, model returns object with discriminator+extra -> after normalize expect discriminator preserved and extra removed only if safe. Also add an integration smoke where sample-app route validates payload and logs the branch chosen.

emily: also check auth/retry interactions: earlier we saw auth retry sometimes returns a truncated body and sanitizer ran on that partial object causing weird picks. Add integration test that simulates 401 then retry with full body in JSON-mode.

rajesh: PR: https://git.redwood/s/sdk-ios/keep-discriminator-in-normalizer (WIP). added tests + changelog entry. pinging sample-app owners for quick validation.

ci-bot: CI queued for PR keep-discriminator-in-normalizer 1430. Sample-app onboarding suite will run.

maria: small nit: document the sanitizer contract in SDK README: json-mode defaults to "preserve discriminators and literal values" unless strictSchema is enabled. helps onboarders understand behavior differences.

emily: agreed. also add a short migration note for mobile integrators: if you relied on unknown-field stripping, add explicit stripUnknownFields flag; default behavior won't drop discriminators.

rajesh: CI green, merged, releasing ios-sdk v0.9.1. ran sample-app smoke, parity confirmed with js/py. closing thread.

maria: nice catch! :tada:
